package neo4jcorpus

import (
	"context"
	"math"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/neo4j/neo4j-go-driver/v5/neo4j"
	"github.com/neo4j/neo4j-go-driver/v5/neo4j/dbtype"
)

// node is the shape the driver hands a decoder: the labels the graph
// stamped on the value, and a Props map holding the Go values
// neo4j.PropertyValue names, and nothing else. Every value in every test
// below is one a Bolt hydrator can actually build — an integer of any
// width arrives as int64, a float of any width as float64, and an array
// of anything but bytes as []any.
//
// The label is a parameter rather than one fixed spelling because the
// emitted decoders guard on it (bd gqlc-2h9w). Under a fixed spelling
// every caller below would have to be handed a value of the wrong type
// for the helper it calls, which is the defect the guard exists to
// refuse — so a battery written that way would test nothing but the
// guard, over and over.
func node(label string, props map[string]any) dbtype.Node {
	return dbtype.Node{Id: 1, ElementId: "4:corpus:1", Labels: []string{label}, Props: props}
}

// relationship is the shape the driver hands an edge decoder. Its Props
// map holds the same Go values a Node's does and it satisfies the same
// dbtype.Entity method set, so on a property decode what separates the two
// carriers is the emission rather than the driver: a decode helper is
// derived per entity, so a narrow or a null one helper was shown to
// survive has not been run through another.
func relationship(props map[string]any) dbtype.Relationship {
	return dbtype.Relationship{
		Id: 2, ElementId: "5:corpus:2",
		StartId: 1, StartElementId: "4:corpus:1",
		EndId: 3, EndElementId: "4:corpus:3",
		Type: "Edgy", Props: props,
	}
}

// typedRelationship is `relationship` under a wire label the caller
// chooses. Only the edge-union dispatch reads that field: a column the
// query committed to one edge type decodes whatever arrives under it
// through that type's helper, whatever the value calls itself.
func typedRelationship(label string, props map[string]any) dbtype.Relationship {
	rel := relationship(props)
	rel.Type = label
	return rel
}

// recordTx is the record shape the driver hands a query method, bound
// through the seam the emission offers for one: Queries.WithTx takes a
// caller-owned transaction, so a method body can be run with no
// connection, no session and no driver behind it.
type recordTx struct{ records []*neo4j.Record }

func (t recordTx) Run(context.Context, string, map[string]any) (neo4j.ResultWithContext, error) {
	return recordResult{records: t.records}, nil
}

type recordResult struct{ records []*neo4j.Record }

func (r recordResult) Collect(context.Context) ([]*neo4j.Record, error) { return r.records, nil }

// queriesOver binds a Queries whose every method reads the given rows,
// one []any of column values per row against the shared key order.
func queriesOver(keys []string, rows ...[]any) *Queries {
	records := make([]*neo4j.Record, 0, len(rows))
	for _, values := range rows {
		records = append(records, &neo4j.Record{Keys: keys, Values: values})
	}
	return new(Queries).WithTx(recordTx{records: records})
}

// paramTx is recordTx that keeps the parameter map it was handed.
//
// It is a distinct type rather than a field on recordTx because the two
// answer opposite questions and only this one has an observation to make:
// every other test here reads a value the driver built, and a bind
// expression is never visible on that side. Run is the only seam it can
// be seen at — after this the map is the driver's, and in the corpus the
// driver is a stub that ignores it.
//
// The map is reached through a pointer because Queries.WithTx takes the
// transaction by value, so a copy is what Run is called on.
type paramTx struct {
	recordTx
	bound *map[string]any
}

func (t paramTx) Run(ctx context.Context, cypher string, params map[string]any) (neo4j.ResultWithContext, error) {
	*t.bound = params
	return t.recordTx.Run(ctx, cypher, params)
}

// queriesRecordingParams binds a Queries that answers with one row of the
// given columns and writes whatever the method bound into *bound.
func queriesRecordingParams(bound *map[string]any, keys []string, values []any) *Queries {
	tx := paramTx{
		recordTx: recordTx{records: []*neo4j.Record{{Keys: keys, Values: values}}},
		bound:    bound,
	}
	return new(Queries).WithTx(tx)
}

// driverRefusal is what neo4j.GetRecordValue says about a record and a key
// it will not read, obtained by asking it rather than by spelling its
// wording out here. A column decode reporting this text has carried the
// driver's own answer to the caller; one reporting anything else has
// either worded a refusal of its own or gone on to a later stage holding
// the zero carrier the driver hands back with the error.
//
// The nil check is not defensive: it is what stops the design alternative
// (returning the empty string on an err-less call) from letting a caller
// assert that a message contains the empty string, which every message does.
func driverRefusal[T neo4j.RecordValue](t *testing.T, keys []string, values []any, key string) string {
	t.Helper()
	_, _, err := neo4j.GetRecordValue[T](&neo4j.Record{Keys: keys, Values: values}, key)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("neo4j.GetRecordValue[%T](%q) = no error, so this record leaves the column's gate nothing to carry", *new(T), key)
	}
	return err.Error()
}

// A list of no declared element shape is the one list whose elements the
// decoder must not narrow. Its declared element type is `any`, a type
// assertion to `any` is false for a nil interface value, and null is
// exactly what such a list exists to be allowed to hold — so narrowing
// it would fail the whole decode on the value it was declared for.
//
// The wants here are also the values the AGE backend produces for the
// same graph data: its agtypeValue maps agtype's inline null to nil (see
// internal/codegen/age/testdata/corpus_test.go.txt, TestAgtypeValue), so
// a caller who moves between the two backends is handed the same list.
func TestBinCarriesNullElements(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeBin(node("Bin", map[string]any{
		"loose": []any{true, nil, 3.5},
		"bag":   []any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(nulls) = error %v", err)
	}
	if want := []any{true, nil, 3.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Loose, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(nulls).Loose = %#v, want %#v", got.Loose, want)
	}
	if got.Bag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(nulls).Bag = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []any{int64(1), nil, "x"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Bag, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(nulls).Bag = %#v, want %#v", *got.Bag, want)
	}
}

// Absence and shape on the same two properties: a nullable list the
// graph does not hold reaches the caller as a nil pointer, an empty one
// as an empty list, and a property holding something that is not a list
// at all is refused rather than carried through.
func TestBinNullabilityAndShape(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeBin(node("Bin", map[string]any{"loose": []any{}}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeBin(absent) = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Loose == nil || len(got.Loose) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(absent).Loose = %#v, want an empty list", got.Loose)
	}
	if got.Bag != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(absent).Bag = %#v, want nil", got.Bag)
	}

	if _, err := decodeBin(node("Bin", map[string]any{"loose": []any{}, "bag": "not a list"})); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(bag: string) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if _, err := decodeBin(node("Bin", map[string]any{})); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeBin(no loose) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// Every other list is narrowed element by element, because the element
// widths the schema declared are not on the wire: the driver hands back
// []any whatever the schema said, so int32 arrives as int64 and float32
// as float64. []byte and time.Time are the two element carriers that do
// arrive as themselves.
func TestListyNarrowsEachElement(t *testing.T) {
	stamp := time.Date(2024, 3, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	got, err := decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags":   []any{"a", "b"},
		"ranks":  []any{int64(1), int64(-2)},
		"blobs":  []any{[]byte{1, 2}, []byte{}},
		"stamps": []any{stamp},
		"depths": []any{0.5, 1.5},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy = error %v", err)
	}
	if want := []string{"a", "b"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Tags = %#v, want %#v", got.Tags, want)
	}
	if want := []int32{1, -2}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Ranks, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Ranks = %#v, want %#v", got.Ranks, want)
	}
	if want := [][]byte{{1, 2}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Blobs, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Blobs = %#v, want %#v", got.Blobs, want)
	}
	if want := []time.Time{stamp}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Stamps, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Stamps = %#v, want %#v", got.Stamps, want)
	}
	if got.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy().Depths = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []float32{0.5, 1.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Depths, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy().Depths = %#v, want %#v", *got.Depths, want)
	}
}

// An empty list is an empty list and not the nil one an absent property
// would reach the caller as. The distinction is the caller's to make, so
// the decoder has to preserve it — and it is the AGE backend's pin too,
// which is what keeps a `len(xs) == 0` check meaning the same thing on
// either backend.
func TestListyEmptyIsNotAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	empty, err := decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{}, "depths": []any{},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(empty) = error %v", err)
	}
	for name, got := range map[string]int{
		"Tags":   len(empty.Tags),
		"Ranks":  len(empty.Ranks),
		"Blobs":  len(empty.Blobs),
		"Stamps": len(empty.Stamps),
	} {
		if got != 0 {
			t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty).%s has %d elements, want 0", name, got)
		}
	}
	if empty.Tags == nil || empty.Ranks == nil || empty.Blobs == nil || empty.Stamps == nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty) reached a caller with a nil list, want empty ones")
	}
	if empty.Depths == nil || *empty.Depths == nil || len(*empty.Depths) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(empty).Depths = %#v, want a pointer to an empty list", empty.Depths)
	}

	absent, err := decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(absent depths) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(absent depths).Depths = %#v, want nil", absent.Depths)
	}
}

// A mis-typed element is refused, and the failure names the property and
// the position, because a list is decoded whole and the caller otherwise
// has nothing to go on.
func TestListyRefusesAMisTypedElement(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{int64(1), "no"},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(ranks: [int, string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	// Subtests rather than a plain loop: corpusSubtests, in the parent
	// module that assembles this one, pins how many of these report a pass,
	// so a case added or dropped here has to be counted there too.
	for _, want := range []string{`"ranks"`, "element 1", "expected int64", "got string"} {
		t.Run(want, func(t *testing.T) {
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
				t.Errorf("decodeListy(ranks: [int, string]) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// A property of no declared shape is read rather than asserted, so every
// value the graph can hold under it reaches the caller as itself — the
// inline null included, which is the one an assertion could not pass.
func TestAnythingReadsWhatTheGraphHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, want := range []any{
		nil, int64(1), 1.5, "x", true,
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		map[string]any{"k": "v"},
	} {
		got, err := decodeAnything(node("Anything", map[string]any{"payload": want}))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("decodeAnything(payload: %#v) = error %v", want, err)
			continue
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Payload, want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeAnything(payload: %#v).Payload = %#v", want, got.Payload)
		}
	}
}

// Under a nullable one the pointer is what separates the two nulls a
// graph can hold: a property the graph does not have at all, and a
// property it holds whose value is null.
func TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull(t *testing.T) {
	absent, err := decodeAnything(node("Anything", map[string]any{"payload": int64(1)}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(no maybe) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(no maybe).Maybe = %#v, want nil", absent.Maybe)
	}

	held, err := decodeAnything(node("Anything", map[string]any{"payload": int64(1), "maybe": nil}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(maybe: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if held.Maybe == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(maybe: null).Maybe = nil, want a pointer to nil")
	}
	if *held.Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(maybe: null).Maybe points at %#v, want nil", *held.Maybe)
	}
}

// The one arm that does not go through the driver still has to fail the
// way the driver fails, or a caller could tell which decode path a
// property took from the error text alone.
func TestAnythingMissingPropertyReadsLikeTheDrivers(t *testing.T) {
	n := node("Anything", map[string]any{})
	decodeErr := func() error {
		_, err := decodeAnything(n)
		return err
	}()
	if decodeErr == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeAnything(no payload) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	_, driverErr := neo4j.GetProperty[int64](n, "payload")
	if driverErr == nil {
		t.Fatalf("neo4j.GetProperty(no payload) = no error")
	}
	if want := "decode Anything.Payload: " + driverErr.Error(); decodeErr.Error() != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeAnything(no payload) = %q, want %q", decodeErr, want)
	}
}

// Scalars narrow from their carriers the same way list elements do, and
// a nullable one the graph does not hold is a nil pointer rather than a
// pointer to the zero value.
func TestScalarNarrows(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeScalar(node("Scalar", map[string]any{
		"id": int64(7), "rank": int64(-3), "active": true, "name": "n", "weight": 0.5, "tally": int64(5),
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Id != 7 || got.Rank != int32(-3) || !got.Active {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar() = %#v", got)
	}
	if got.Name == nil || *got.Name != "n" {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar().Name = %#v, want \"n\"", got.Name)
	}
	if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != float32(0.5) {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar().Weight = %#v, want 0.5", got.Weight)
	}

	absent, err := decodeScalar(node("Scalar", map[string]any{"id": int64(7), "rank": int64(0), "active": false, "tally": int64(0)}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(absent) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Name != nil || absent.Weight != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar(absent) = %#v, want nil nullables", absent)
	}
}

// The widths above, narrowed off a Relationship's Props rather than a
// Node's: a scalar and a list element that both arrive wider than the
// schema declared, a nullable scalar and a nullable list that arrive
// wider still, a list of no declared element shape holding the null such
// a list exists to carry, a list whose elements arrive as themselves and
// are asserted rather than narrowed, and a property of no declared shape
// read as it arrived. There is no list of lists among them, and there
// cannot be: ADR 0035 leaves no neo4j stored property of that width to
// declare.
func TestEdgyNarrowsOverARelationship(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(map[string]any{
		"rank":    int64(-3),
		"ranks":   []any{int64(1), int64(-2)},
		"blobs":   []any{[]byte{1, 2}, []byte{}},
		"payload": map[string]any{"k": "v"},
		"loose":   []any{true, nil, 3.5},
		"depths":  []any{0.5, 1.5},
		"weight":  0.5,
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Rank = %#v, want -3", got.Rank)
	}
	if want := []int32{1, -2}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Ranks, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Ranks = %#v, want %#v", got.Ranks, want)
	}
	// The elements the driver hands back already the declared width. The
	// walk asserts to []byte and appends what it asserted, and an empty
	// element has to survive that as itself rather than as a nil slice.
	if want := [][]byte{{1, 2}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Blobs, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Blobs = %#v, want %#v", got.Blobs, want)
	}
	if want := map[string]any{"k": "v"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Payload, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Payload = %#v, want %#v", got.Payload, want)
	}
	if got.Loose == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy().Loose = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []any{true, nil, 3.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Loose, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Loose = %#v, want %#v", *got.Loose, want)
	}
	if got.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy().Depths = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []float32{0.5, 1.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*got.Depths, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Depths = %#v, want %#v", *got.Depths, want)
	}
	if got.Weight == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy().Weight = nil, want 0.5")
	}
	if *got.Weight != float32(0.5) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy().Weight = %#v, want 0.5", *got.Weight)
	}
}

// A Relationship property the schema did not declare that way is refused,
// and the failure names the struct field and — inside a list — the
// property and the position. The wording is per-entity text the emission
// writes out for each decode helper it derives, so a helper shown to word
// its refusal one way leaves the others unmeasured.
func TestEdgyRefusesWhatTheSchemaDidNotDeclare(t *testing.T) {
	full := func() map[string]any {
		return map[string]any{
			"rank": int64(0), "ranks": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "payload": int64(1),
		}
	}
	with := func(key string, value any) map[string]any {
		props := full()
		props[key] = value
		return props
	}
	without := func(key string) map[string]any {
		props := full()
		delete(props, key)
		return props
	}

	_, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(with("ranks", []any{int64(1), "no"})))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(ranks: [int, string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"decode Edgy.Ranks", `"ranks"`, "element 1", "expected int64", "got string"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(ranks: [int, string]) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// An element the walk asserts to rather than narrows names its own
	// carrier in the refusal, not the []any the property arrived as.
	_, err = decodeEdgy(relationship(with("blobs", []any{[]byte{1}, "no"})))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(blobs: [bytes, string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"decode Edgy.Blobs", `"blobs"`, "element 1", "expected []byte", "got string"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(blobs: [bytes, string]) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	_, err = decodeEdgy(relationship(with("loose", "not a list")))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(loose: string) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "decode Edgy.Loose"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(loose: string) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}

	// A nullable list walks its elements inside the block its null gate
	// opens, so its refusal is emitted separately from the non-nullable
	// one above.
	_, err = decodeEdgy(relationship(with("depths", []any{0.5, "no"})))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(depths: [float, string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"decode Edgy.Depths", `"depths"`, "element 1", "expected float64", "got string"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(depths: [float, string]) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	_, err = decodeEdgy(relationship(with("weight", int64(1))))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(weight: int) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "decode Edgy.Weight"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(weight: int) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}

	// The two non-nullable arms report a missing property through
	// different code: rank/ranks/blobs reach neo4j.GetProperty and carry
	// its own miss, payload is read off Props directly and carries the
	// emission's own wording.
	for _, key := range []string{"rank", "ranks", "blobs", "payload"} {
		if _, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(without(key))); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(no %s) = no error, want a refusal", key)
		}
	}
}

// Absence, emptiness and a held null on the relationship carrier. A
// nullable the relationship does not hold is a nil pointer, an empty list
// stays distinguishable from an absent one, and a non-nullable property
// of no declared shape whose value is null is carried rather than refused
// — its arm reads the Props map, where a key holding nil is present.
func TestEdgyKeepsAbsentApartFromEmptyOverARelationship(t *testing.T) {
	absent, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(map[string]any{
		"rank": int64(0), "ranks": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "payload": nil,
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(absent) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Loose != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(absent).Loose = %#v, want nil", absent.Loose)
	}
	if absent.Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(absent).Depths = %#v, want nil", absent.Depths)
	}
	if absent.Weight != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(absent).Weight = %#v, want nil", absent.Weight)
	}
	if absent.Payload != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(payload: null).Payload = %#v, want nil", absent.Payload)
	}
	if absent.Ranks == nil || len(absent.Ranks) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(absent).Ranks = %#v, want an empty list", absent.Ranks)
	}

	empty, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(map[string]any{
		"rank": int64(0), "ranks": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "payload": int64(1),
		"loose": []any{}, "depths": []any{},
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(empty lists) = error %v", err)
	}
	if empty.Loose == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(empty lists).Loose = nil, want a pointer to an empty list")
	}
	if *empty.Loose == nil || len(*empty.Loose) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(empty lists).Loose = %#v, want a pointer to an empty list", *empty.Loose)
	}
	if empty.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(empty lists).Depths = nil, want a pointer to an empty list")
	}
	if *empty.Depths == nil || len(*empty.Depths) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(empty lists).Depths = %#v, want a pointer to an empty list", *empty.Depths)
	}
}

// A query column carrying a list of no declared element shape is the
// same claim as TestBinCarriesNullElements, one emission over: a column
// is decoded through neo4j.GetRecordValue and a property through the
// Props map, so the two paths narrow independently and a null that
// survives one can still fail the other.
func TestBinColumnsCarryNullElements(t *testing.T) {
	q := queriesOver([]string{"loose", "bag"}, []any{
		[]any{true, nil, 3.5},
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
	})
	got, err := q.BinColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls) returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := []any{true, nil, 3.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Loose, want) {
		t.Errorf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Loose = %#v, want %#v", row.Loose, want)
	}
	if row.Bag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Bag = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []any{int64(1), nil, "x"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Bag, want) {
		t.Errorf("BinColumns(nulls)[0].Bag = %#v, want %#v", *row.Bag, want)
	}
}

// The control on the test above: a column whose elements do have a
// declared width still narrows to it, so "carry the element as it
// arrived" is the rule for the one width that has no narrower carrier
// and not a rule the emission applies everywhere. Both directions are
// here — []byte arrives as itself and is kept, float64 arrives wider
// than the declared float32 and is narrowed — because a decoder that
// carried everything bare would pass on the first alone.
//
// The projection carries two non-nullable list columns rather than one
// because the accumulator each of them builds is a local of the row
// assembly's own scope: under a name shared between them the second
// declaration is `no new variables on left side of :=`, and the
// projection that reaches it is the one no fixture had. A nullable list
// column does not reach it, because its accumulator sits inside the
// `if` its null gate opens.
func TestListyColumnsNarrowEachElement(t *testing.T) {
	q := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{
		[]any{"a", "b"},
		[]any{[]byte{1, 2}, []byte{}},
		[]any{0.5, 1.5},
	})
	got, err := q.ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := []string{"a", "b"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Tags = %#v, want %#v", row.Tags, want)
	}
	if want := [][]byte{{1, 2}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Blobs, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Blobs = %#v, want %#v", row.Blobs, want)
	}
	if row.Depths == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns()[0].Depths = nil, want a list")
	}
	if want := []float32{0.5, 1.5}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*row.Depths, want) {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns()[0].Depths = %#v, want %#v", *row.Depths, want)
	}

	// A null column and an empty list stay distinguishable here too, and
	// on this path the distinction is the driver's own: GetRecordValue
	// reports a held null through its second result rather than through
	// the value, so a decoder reading only the value cannot tell them
	// apart.
	null, err := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{[]any{}, []any{}, nil}).ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(depths: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(null) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(depths: null) returned %d rows, want 1", len(null))
	}
	if null[0].Tags == nil || len(null[0].Tags) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Tags = %#v, want an empty list", null[0].Tags)
	}
	if null[0].Blobs == nil || len(null[0].Blobs) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Blobs = %#v, want an empty list", null[0].Blobs)
	}
	if null[0].Depths != nil {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(depths: null)[0].Depths = %#v, want nil", null[0].Depths)
	}

	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}, []any{
		[]any{}, []any{"no"}, []any{},
	}).ListyColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(blobs: [string]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// A list column reads its value through neo4j.GetRecordValue[[]any], and
// the same gate the entity columns carry is what reports the driver's
// refusal here. The mis-typed element above is a different gate — the
// element loop's — and it can only be reached by a value this one let
// through, so nothing it pins carries back to this one.
//
// What a dropped gate costs is larger on this arm than on the entity arm:
// the zero []any it passes on is an empty list, the element loop walks it
// without complaint, and the caller is handed an empty list for a value
// the driver refused. So both cases below report the rows on failure,
// because the failure to expect is a row rather than a mis-worded error.
//
// They assert the message anyway, and it is not redundant with that: a
// dropped gate is not the only way to lose the driver's answer, and a gate
// that fires in words of its own satisfies any test that asks only whether
// something came back.
func TestListColumnRefusalsCarryTheDriversError(t *testing.T) {
	// A column holding something that is not a list at all. The two
	// columns after it are well-formed, so the refusal is this column's.
	keys := []string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"}
	notAList := []any{"not a list", []any{}, []any{}}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, notAList).ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(tags: string) = %#v, want a refusal", got)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"tags"`, driverRefusal[[]any](t, keys, notAList, "tags")} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("ListyColumns(tags: string) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// A record that does not hold the key the query projected, which the
	// driver reports through the same error rather than as a held null —
	// the null it does report is the one ListyColumns(depths: null) above
	// reads through isNil.
	absent := []string{"nope", "blobs", "depths"}
	held := []any{[]any{}, []any{}, []any{}}
	got, err = queriesOver(absent, held).ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(no tags) = %#v, want a refusal", got)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"tags"`, driverRefusal[[]any](t, absent, held, "tags")} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("ListyColumns(no tags) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// The element loop nests once per declared list depth, and every level
// of it accumulates into a local of its own. Under a name shared between
// the levels the inner declaration shadows the one the level above
// appends to, so that accumulator and appended value become one
// identifier and the emitted package does not compile. A depth of three
// is the first that reaches it, being the first that puts one such
// declaration inside another.
//
// The two sibling depth-two columns are the control: their loops are
// disjoint blocks, so what the deep columns are refused for is the depth
// and not the count. The two sibling depth-THREE columns make the same
// control one level down, where the emitter's suffixing has to hold for
// an accumulator nested inside another.
//
// These columns are spelled over literals, so they are all non-nullable
// and the nullable arm a nested column used to reach is not measured
// here — see the note above NestColumns in the queries file for why no
// declared property can supply one on this backend.
func TestNestColumnsAccumulateAtEveryDepth(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"cube", "lhs", "rhs", "deep"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		[]any{[]any{[]any{int64(1), int64(2)}, []any{}}, []any{}},
		[]any{[]any{int64(3)}, []any{int64(4), int64(5)}},
		[]any{[]any{"a"}, []any{}},
		[]any{[]any{[]any{"x"}}},
	}).NestColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(nested) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("NestColumns(nested) returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if want := [][][]int64{{{1, 2}, {}}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Cube, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Cube = %#v, want %#v", row.Cube, want)
	}
	if want := [][]int64{{3}, {4, 5}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Lhs, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Lhs = %#v, want %#v", row.Lhs, want)
	}
	if want := [][]string{{"a"}, {}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Rhs, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Rhs = %#v, want %#v", row.Rhs, want)
	}
	if want := [][][]string{{{"x"}}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.Deep, want) {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(nested)[0].Deep = %#v, want %#v", row.Deep, want)
	}

	if _, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		[]any{[]any{int64(1)}}, []any{}, []any{}, []any{},
	}).NestColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("NestColumns(cube: [[int]]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// A column whose declared width is ANY VALUE is read rather than
// asserted, the same claim TestAnythingReadsWhatTheGraphHolds makes of
// the property one emission over. `any` is a member of neither
// neo4j.PropertyValue nor neo4j.RecordValue, so the column has no
// constrained driver entry point to go through at all — and the null it
// exists to carry is the one value such an entry point could not have
// been written to carry.
//
// Null is not in this table because payload is NOT NULL, and what a
// non-nullable column does with a null is refuse it — see
// TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull, which holds both halves of that.
func TestAnythingColumnsReadWhatTheGraphHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, want := range []any{
		int64(1), 1.5, "x", true,
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		map[string]any{"k": "v"},
	} {
		got, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{want, want}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v) = error %v", want, err)
			continue
		}
		if len(got) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v) returned %d rows, want 1", want, len(got))
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got[0].Payload, want) {
			t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(payload: %#v)[0].Payload = %#v", want, got[0].Payload)
		}
	}
}

// The nullable one carries the graph's null in its pointer. A record
// holds a key for every column the query projected, so a pointer spent
// on the missing key the Props map can have would be a pointer that is
// never nil — a null the caller has no way to read. This is the one
// place the column path and the entity path answer differently, and
// TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull is the other half of the pair.
func TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull(t *testing.T) {
	null, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{int64(1), nil}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(null) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null) returned %d rows, want 1", len(null))
	}
	if null[0].Maybe != nil {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(maybe: null)[0].Maybe = %#v, want nil", null[0].Maybe)
	}

	held, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{int64(1), "v"}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\") = error %v", err)
	}
	if held[0].Maybe == nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\")[0].Maybe = nil, want a pointer")
	}
	if *held[0].Maybe != any("v") {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(maybe: \"v\")[0].Maybe points at %#v, want \"v\"", *held[0].Maybe)
	}

	// A column the record does not hold at all is neither of those: the
	// resolver committed it, so its absence is the driver disagreeing
	// with the plan rather than a value the graph held.
	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"payload"}, []any{int64(1)}).AnythingColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(no maybe) = no error, want a refusal")
	}

	// The non-nullable one refuses it instead. Every other width gets
	// this for free — its Go type has no nil to return — so the refusal
	// is the whole of what NOT NULL means for a column typed `any`.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"payload", "maybe"}, []any{nil, nil}).AnythingColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnythingColumns(payload: null) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "non-nullable but arrived null") ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "payload") {
		t.Errorf("AnythingColumns(payload: null) = error %v, want it to name payload and its non-nullability", err)
	}
}

// ANY PROPERTY VALUE is a second spelling of the same declared width as
// ANY VALUE — internal/schema/gql/propertytype.go maps "ANY VALUE",
// "ANY", "PROPERTY VALUE" and "ANY PROPERTY VALUE" all onto
// graph.TypeAnyPropertyValue — and the emission is therefore expected to
// be the same record.Get lane the two tests above run. Expected is not
// measured: codegen reads a graph.PropertyType, so the only thing that
// could put the two spellings on different lanes is a change to that
// mapping, and no test in this repo held the column path against the
// second spelling at all (bd gqlc-v7vu, found reviewing gqlc-dcap).
//
// So this pair is not a claim that the two widths differ. It is the row
// that goes red if they ever stop agreeing, held one emission down from
// the schema fixture that pins the same pair as golden bytes: golden
// bytes move under -update and this does not.
//
// Null is absent from this table for the reason it is absent from
// TestAnythingColumnsReadWhatTheGraphHolds's: badge is NOT NULL, and the
// refusal it owes a null lives in the null half below.
func TestAnyPropertyValueColumnsReadWhatTheGraphHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, want := range []any{
		int64(1), 1.5, "x", true,
		[]any{int64(1), nil, "x"},
		map[string]any{"k": "v"},
	} {
		got, err := queriesOver([]string{"badge", "tag"}, []any{want, want}).AnyPropColumns(t.Context())
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(badge: %#v) = error %v", want, err)
			continue
		}
		if len(got) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(badge: %#v) returned %d rows, want 1", want, len(got))
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got[0].Badge, want) {
			t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(badge: %#v)[0].Badge = %#v", want, got[0].Badge)
		}
	}
}

// The null half, held apart from the read half for the reason
// TestAnythingColumnsCarryTheirNull gives: a record holds a key for every
// column the query projected, so the nullable column's pointer has only
// the graph's null to spend itself on, and a missing key is the driver
// disagreeing with the plan rather than a value.
func TestAnyPropertyValueColumnsCarryTheirNull(t *testing.T) {
	null, err := queriesOver([]string{"badge", "tag"}, []any{int64(1), nil}).AnyPropColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(tag: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(null) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(tag: null) returned %d rows, want 1", len(null))
	}
	if null[0].Tag != nil {
		t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(tag: null)[0].Tag = %#v, want nil", null[0].Tag)
	}

	held, err := queriesOver([]string{"badge", "tag"}, []any{int64(1), "v"}).AnyPropColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(tag: \"v\") = error %v", err)
	}
	if held[0].Tag == nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(tag: \"v\")[0].Tag = nil, want a pointer")
	}
	if *held[0].Tag != any("v") {
		t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(tag: \"v\")[0].Tag points at %#v, want \"v\"", *held[0].Tag)
	}

	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"badge"}, []any{int64(1)}).AnyPropColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(no tag) = no error, want a refusal")
	}

	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"badge", "tag"}, []any{nil, nil}).AnyPropColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("AnyPropColumns(badge: null) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "non-nullable but arrived null") ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "badge") {
		t.Errorf("AnyPropColumns(badge: null) = error %v, want it to name badge and its non-nullability", err)
	}
}

// scalarProps, listyProps and edgyProps are the driver values the three
// entities above are decoded from, as a whole-entity column carries
// them: a Props map on one dbtype value rather than a column per
// property. Each carries every property its type declared NOT NULL, so
// what a test varies is the one thing it is about.
func scalarProps() map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{"id": int64(7), "rank": int64(-3), "active": true, "name": "n", "tally": int64(5)}
}

func listyProps() map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{"a"}, "ranks": []any{int64(1)},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}
}

func edgyProps() map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{
		"rank": int64(-3), "ranks": []any{int64(1)}, "blobs": []any{}, "payload": int64(1),
	}
}

// A whole node and a whole edge projected as columns rather than
// property by property. The decode helper each one reaches is the
// entity's own — the same helper TestScalarNarrows and
// TestEdgyNarrowsOverARelationship run — but what hands it the driver
// value is the column path: neo4j.GetRecordValue asserts to dbtype.Node
// or dbtype.Relationship and the helper takes it from there, so the
// carrier a column commits to is a decision this projection makes and
// the entity path does not.
//
// The three columns are decoded into one Row struct, which is where the
// carrier locals collide if they are not numbered: two node columns in
// one row assembly is the projection that reaches that, and the edge
// between them is a third carrier local under the same rule.
func TestEntityColumnsDecodeWholeEntities(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := queriesOver([]string{"s", "e", "l"}, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), relationship(edgyProps()), node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("EntityColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("EntityColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if row.S.Id != 7 || row.S.Rank != int32(-3) || !row.S.Active {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].S = %#v", row.S)
	}
	if row.S.Name == nil || *row.S.Name != "n" {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].S.Name = %#v, want \"n\"", row.S.Name)
	}
	if row.E.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].E.Rank = %#v, want -3", row.E.Rank)
	}
	if want := []int32{1}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.E.Ranks, want) {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].E.Ranks = %#v, want %#v", row.E.Ranks, want)
	}
	if row.E.Payload != any(int64(1)) {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].E.Payload = %#v, want 1", row.E.Payload)
	}
	if want := []string{"a"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.L.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].L.Tags = %#v, want %#v", row.L.Tags, want)
	}
	if want := []int32{1}; !reflect.DeepEqual(row.L.Ranks, want) {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns()[0].L.Ranks = %#v, want %#v", row.L.Ranks, want)
	}

	// The same three values under two of the same keys, swapped, are
	// refused rather than decoded into a row. The fact of the refusal is
	// all this case reads: which stage produced it is what
	// TestEntityColumnRefusalsCarryTheDriversError below settles, out of
	// this same swap. The carrier is settled before either stage runs —
	// emit the edge column's read as dbtype.Node and the nested module
	// stops compiling, so this case never runs.
	if _, err := queriesOver([]string{"s", "e", "l"}, []any{
		relationship(edgyProps()), node("Scalar", scalarProps()), node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).EntityColumns(t.Context()); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("EntityColumns(s: relationship) = no error, want a refusal")
	}

	// A null under a non-nullable entity column is refused rather than
	// carried as the struct's zero composite, which is what the caller
	// would otherwise be handed for a row the graph does not have.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"s", "e", "l"}, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), nil, node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EntityColumns(e: null) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, "non-nullable"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("EntityColumns(e: null) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// The helper really runs on the column's value: a node whose Props
	// do not satisfy the entity it was projected as fails the whole
	// decode, and the failure names both the column and the field.
	missing := scalarProps()
	delete(missing, "rank")
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"s", "e", "l"}, []any{
		node("Scalar", missing), relationship(edgyProps()), node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EntityColumns(s: no rank) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"s"`, "decode Scalar.Rank"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("EntityColumns(s: no rank) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// An entity column reads its value through neo4j.GetRecordValue, which
// refuses a key the record does not hold and a value that is not the
// carrier the column committed to. This is that refusal reaching the
// caller: the column's error gate carries the driver's answer, and it
// carries it before the entity's decode helper is handed a value the
// driver has already rejected.
//
// TestEntityColumnsDecodeWholeEntities above hands the row the same swapped
// values, but asks only whether some error came back — and both a gate that
// reports the driver's refusal and a gate that drops it return one.
// Dropping it passes on the zero carrier, whose empty Props map the decode
// helper then refuses on the first property it looks for, so the caller is
// told a property is missing from a graph value that never arrived. That
// is a refusal for a neighbouring reason, which is why the checks here read
// the message rather than stopping at the fact of an error, and why one of
// them is on what the message must not say.
func TestEntityColumnRefusalsCarryTheDriversError(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"s", "e", "l"}
	// unreached names the decode helper the column would reach if its gate
	// let the rejected value through; naming the helper's prefix rather
	// than one property keeps the check on which stage answered.
	check := func(what, column, want, unreached string, err error) {
		t.Helper()
		if err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s = no error, want a refusal", what)
		}
		for _, w := range []string{column, want} {
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), w) {
				t.Errorf("%s = %q, want it to mention %s", what, err, w)
			}
		}
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), unreached) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want the column's own gate to refuse it before %s runs", what, err, unreached)
		}
	}

	// A relationship under a node column.
	sIsRel := []any{relationship(edgyProps()), node("Scalar", scalarProps()), node("Listy", listyProps())}
	_, err := queriesOver(keys, sIsRel).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	check("EntityColumns(s: relationship)", `"s"`,
		driverRefusal[dbtype.Node](t, keys, sIsRel, "s"), "decode Scalar.", err)

	// A node under an edge column. What this adds to the case above is the
	// position rather than the carrier: which carrier each column commits
	// to is already held by the nested module's own compile, since a column
	// decoded to the wrong one does not typecheck against its decode
	// helper. This one is the gate reached at a column that is not the
	// first, after the column ahead of it decoded — the case above returns
	// at `s` and never gets here.
	eIsNode := []any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), node("Scalar", scalarProps()), node("Listy", listyProps())}
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, eIsNode).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	check("EntityColumns(e: node)", `"e"`,
		driverRefusal[dbtype.Relationship](t, keys, eIsNode, "e"), "decode Edgy.", err)

	// A record that does not hold the key the query projected. The driver
	// tells absence and wrong type apart, but the column has one gate for
	// both, so a gate that drops the error drops this too.
	absent := []string{"nope", "e", "l"}
	held := []any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), relationship(edgyProps()), node("Listy", listyProps())}
	_, err = queriesOver(absent, held).EntityColumns(t.Context())
	check("EntityColumns(no s)", `"s"`,
		driverRefusal[dbtype.Node](t, absent, held, "s"), "decode Scalar.", err)
}

// An edge column whose pattern admits more than one edge type is decoded
// through a dispatch on the wire label, because a relationship carries
// its label and its properties and not the endpoint types that told the
// two candidates apart in the schema. The column's Go type is the sealed
// interface both candidates carry a marker for, so what a caller reads
// the decode's answer out of is a type assertion — and that is what
// makes which candidate ran observable here.
func TestEdgeUnionColumnDispatchesOnTheWireLabel(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := queriesOver([]string{"e"},
		[]any{typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps())},
		[]any{typedRelationship("Edgier", map[string]any{"tag": "t"})},
	).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn returned %d rows, want 2", len(got))
	}
	edgy, ok := got[0].(Edgy)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn()[0] = %T, want Edgy", got[0])
	}
	if edgy.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn()[0].(Edgy).Rank = %#v, want -3", edgy.Rank)
	}
	edgier, ok := got[1].(Edgier)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn()[1] = %T, want Edgier", got[1])
	}
	if edgier.Tag != "t" {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn()[1].(Edgier).Tag = %#v, want \"t\"", edgier.Tag)
	}

	// The label picks the helper, not the Props map: Edgy's own
	// properties under Edgier's label reach decodeEdgier, which has no
	// tag to read. A dispatch that guessed from the shape of what
	// arrived would decode this one and pass.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{typedRelationship("Edgier", edgyProps())}).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn(Edgier: Edgy's props) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "decode Edgier.Tag"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn(Edgier: Edgy's props) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}

	// A label no candidate carries is refused rather than dropped, and
	// the refusal quotes the label so the author can see which value in
	// their graph the pattern reached.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{typedRelationship("Nope", edgyProps())}).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn(type: Nope) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, `"Nope"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn(type: Nope) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// This column is read through record.Get, which hands back a bare
	// (any, bool): the bool reports key absence, and both a held null
	// and a value of the wrong dynamic type arrive as an untyped any.
	// So each refusal below is worded by the emission itself — the
	// non-relationship off its own type assertion, the held null off
	// its own nil check, the missing key off Get's bool.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{node("Scalar", scalarProps())}).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn(e: node) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "expected dbtype.Relationship"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn(e: node) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}

	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{nil}).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn(e: null) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "non-nullable"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn(e: null) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}

	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"other"}, []any{typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps())}).EdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("EdgeUnionColumn(no e) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "missing from record"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("EdgeUnionColumn(no e) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}
}

// A decoder handed a value of another entity's type refuses it rather
// than filling the struct from whatever Props happen to be there. This
// is the defect bd gqlc-2h9w records: Scalar and Edgy both declare a
// non-nullable INT32 named rank, so before the guard landed
// decodeScalar(a Listy node) and decodeEdgy(an Edgier relationship)
// were free to succeed on the overlap and report no error.
//
// The overlap is what makes this a behaviour test rather than a reading
// of the emission. The props handed over below are the ones the target
// entity itself declares, so nothing in the property reads can fail:
// only the label check stands between the caller and a populated struct
// built out of the wrong graph value.
func TestDecodersRefuseAValueOfAnotherType(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := decodeScalar(node("Listy", scalarProps()))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(a Listy node) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"Scalar", "Listy"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeScalar(a Listy node) = %q, want it to name %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	_, err = decodeEdgy(typedRelationship("Edgier", edgyProps()))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(an Edgier relationship) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"Edgy", "Edgier"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(an Edgier relationship) = %q, want it to name %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// The node guard is containment, not equality. A deployment stamps
// labels the schema never declared — a lifecycle marker, a tenant tag —
// and a node still carrying the key label the schema names is still that
// entity. An equality check against the key set would refuse it, which
// would make the guard a second defect rather than a fix for one.
//
// The refusal half is here as well as in the test above so that the two
// sit side by side: what moves between them is one extra label on the
// value, and the verdict flips on the key label alone.
func TestNodeDecoderAcceptsLabelsTheSchemaDoesNotDeclare(t *testing.T) {
	extra := node("Scalar", scalarProps())
	extra.Labels = []string{"Archived", "Scalar", "Tenant7"}
	got, err := decodeScalar(extra)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(a Scalar carrying extra labels) = error %v", err)
	}
	if got.Id != 7 || got.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar(a Scalar carrying extra labels) = %#v", got)
	}

	none := node("Scalar", scalarProps())
	none.Labels = []string{"Archived", "Tenant7"}
	if _, err := decodeScalar(none); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(a node carrying neither the key label nor nothing) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
}

// A zero-labelled value is the other end of the same axis: the driver
// hands back a Node whose Labels slice is empty, and a guard written as
// a loop over that slice reports nothing wrong if it forgets that the
// empty case is a miss. Held separately because the loop is the shape
// the emitter writes and an empty range body never runs.
func TestNodeDecoderRefusesAnUnlabelledNode(t *testing.T) {
	bare := node("Scalar", scalarProps())
	bare.Labels = nil
	_, err := decodeScalar(bare)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(an unlabelled node) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "Scalar"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeScalar(an unlabelled node) = %q, want it to name %s", err, want)
	}
}

// A column of a declared scalar width is the one column arm that reads
// through neo4j.GetRecordValue[T] for a T that is neither []any nor a
// dbtype value: bool and string ride their own carriers, an INT32 rides
// int64 and a FLOAT32 rides float64, and the narrowing is a plain Go
// conversion the emission writes after the read.
//
// Nothing the list and entity columns pin reaches it. Those instantiate
// GetRecordValue at []any, dbtype.Node and dbtype.Relationship, which
// until this projection existed were the only three instantiations the
// corpus produced at all — so the arm could be deleted whole and every
// row stayed green (bd gqlc-8bl0).
func TestScalarColumnsNarrowTheirCarriers(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"id", "rank", "active", "name", "weight", "tally"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{int64(7), int64(-3), true, "n", 0.5, int64(5)}).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	row := got[0]
	if row.Id != int64(7) || row.Rank != int32(-3) || !row.Active {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns()[0] = %#v", row)
	}
	if row.Name == nil || *row.Name != "n" {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns()[0].Name = %#v, want \"n\"", row.Name)
	}
	if row.Weight == nil || *row.Weight != float32(0.5) {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns()[0].Weight = %#v, want 0.5", row.Weight)
	}

	// A nullable one the graph holds as null is a nil pointer rather than
	// a pointer to the zero the driver hands back beside its isNil.
	null, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{int64(7), int64(-3), true, nil, nil, int64(5)}).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns(name: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if null[0].Name != nil {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(name: null)[0].Name = %#v, want nil", null[0].Name)
	}
	if null[0].Weight != nil {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(name: null)[0].Weight = %#v, want nil", null[0].Weight)
	}

	// A non-nullable one the graph holds as null is refused rather than
	// carried as the carrier's zero, which is what the caller would
	// otherwise read as a rank of 0.
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, []any{int64(7), nil, true, "n", 0.5, int64(5)}).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns(rank: null) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"rank"`, "non-nullable"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(rank: null) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// The error gate this arm opens with, which no row reached before this
// one. What a dropped gate costs here is silence rather than a
// mis-worded error: neo4j.GetRecordValue reports a wrong dynamic type
// and a missing key by returning its zero carrier with isNil FALSE, so
// the isNil gate below it never fires and the caller is handed a rank of
// 0 and a nil error for a column the driver refused.
//
// So the fact of an error is itself load-bearing here, and the message
// checks are what separate this gate from a refusal of a neighbouring
// kind: the positive is the driver's own wording, asked of the driver
// rather than spelled out, and the negative is the null gate one line
// down — a gate rewritten to route a type disagreement through that one
// would report a column the graph holds as having arrived null.
func TestScalarColumnRefusalsCarryTheDriversError(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"id", "rank", "active", "name", "weight", "tally"}
	check := func(what string, got []ScalarColumnsRow, err error, want string) {
		t.Helper()
		if err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s = %#v, want a refusal", what, got)
		}
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `"rank"`) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want it to name the column %q", what, err, "rank")
		}
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want it to carry the driver's answer %q", what, err, want)
		}
		if unwanted := "non-nullable"; strings.Contains(err.Error(), unwanted) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want the column's own error gate to refuse it rather than the null gate below it", what, err)
		}
	}

	// A value of a type the carrier does not admit. The columns around it
	// are well-formed, so the refusal is this column's.
	misTyped := []any{int64(7), "not an int", true, "n", 0.5, int64(5)}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, misTyped).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	check("ScalarColumns(rank: string)", got, err, driverRefusal[int64](t, keys, misTyped, "rank"))

	// A record that does not hold the key the query projected, which the
	// driver reports through the same gate — and which it reports with
	// isNil false, so nothing further down the arm can catch it either.
	absent := []string{"id", "nope", "active", "name", "weight", "tally"}
	held := []any{int64(7), int64(-3), true, "n", 0.5, int64(5)}
	got, err = queriesOver(absent, held).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	check("ScalarColumns(no rank)", got, err, driverRefusal[int64](t, absent, held, "rank"))
}

// A whole-entity column the query made optional. The non-nullable arm is
// TestEntityColumnsDecodeWholeEntities'; this is the other one, which
// wraps the decoded struct in a pointer and skips the decode entirely
// when the driver reports the column null. Both carriers are here
// because the arm is written once and instantiated twice — dbtype.Node
// for a node column and dbtype.Relationship for an edge one — and a
// pointer wrap shown to work on one says nothing about the other.
func TestOptionalEntityColumnsCarryTheirNull(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"s", "e", "l"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), relationship(edgyProps()), node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).OptionalEntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	if got[0].E == nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns()[0].E = nil, want a pointer to an Edgy")
	}
	if got[0].E.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns()[0].E.Rank = %#v, want -3", got[0].E.Rank)
	}
	if got[0].L == nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns()[0].L = nil, want a pointer to a Listy")
	}
	if want := []string{"a"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got[0].L.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns()[0].L.Tags = %#v, want %#v", got[0].L.Tags, want)
	}

	// The optional half the pattern did not match. Both nullable columns
	// arrive null in the same row, so what is asserted is each pointer
	// rather than the fact that some pointer was nil.
	null, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), nil, nil}).OptionalEntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns(e, l: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if null[0].E != nil {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns(e: null)[0].E = %#v, want nil", null[0].E)
	}
	if null[0].L != nil {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns(l: null)[0].L = %#v, want nil", null[0].L)
	}
	if null[0].S.Id != int64(7) {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns(e, l: null)[0].S = %#v, want the row's own node decoded", null[0].S)
	}

	// The decode helper really runs inside the non-null branch: a
	// relationship whose Props do not satisfy the entity fails the whole
	// row rather than landing as a pointer to a half-filled struct.
	missing := edgyProps()
	delete(missing, "rank")
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), relationship(missing), node("Listy", listyProps()),
	}).OptionalEntityColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEntityColumns(e: no rank) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, "decode Edgy.Rank"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("OptionalEntityColumns(e: no rank) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// An edge-union column the query made optional, decoded beside a second
// column. Two arms meet here that no row reached before: the nullable
// one, which assigns the nil interface rather than dispatching, and the
// multi-column row assembly, whose locals carry a numeric suffix so two
// columns in one row never share the raw / rel / entity bindings.
func TestOptionalEdgeUnionColumnCarriesItsNull(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"s", "e"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys,
		[]any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps())},
		[]any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), typedRelationship("Edgier", map[string]any{"tag": "t"})},
		[]any{node("Scalar", scalarProps()), nil},
	).OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn returned %d rows, want 3", len(got))
	}
	edgy, ok := got[0].E.(Edgy)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[0].E = %T, want Edgy", got[0].E)
	}
	if edgy.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[0].E.(Edgy).Rank = %#v, want -3", edgy.Rank)
	}
	edgier, ok := got[1].E.(Edgier)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[1].E = %T, want Edgier", got[1].E)
	}
	if edgier.Tag != "t" {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[1].E.(Edgier).Tag = %#v, want \"t\"", edgier.Tag)
	}
	if got[2].E != nil {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[2].E = %#v, want nil", got[2].E)
	}
	// The column beside it decoded in every row, which is what says the
	// null arm assigned rather than returned.
	for i, row := range got {
		if row.S.Id != int64(7) {
			t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn()[%d].S = %#v, want the row's own node decoded", i, row.S)
		}
	}

	// Nullable buys the null and nothing else: a label no candidate
	// carries is still refused, and it is refused inside the branch the
	// non-nil value took.
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), typedRelationship("Nope", edgyProps()),
	}).OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(type: Nope) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, `"Nope"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(type: Nope) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// A value that is not a relationship at all takes the same branch and
	// is refused by the type assertion the dispatch opens with.
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, []any{
		node("Scalar", scalarProps()), node("Scalar", scalarProps()),
	}).OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(e: node) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	if want := "expected dbtype.Relationship"; !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Errorf("OptionalEdgeUnionColumn(e: node) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
	}
}

// A whole entity inside a LIST column. A variable-length relationship
// pattern is what reaches it: the binding resolves to a list of edges,
// so the column reads []any through the driver and hands each element to
// the entity's own decode helper — the element loop's entity arm, which
// is a different emission from the entity COLUMN arm above and shares no
// line with it.
func TestVarLengthEdgeColumnDecodesEveryElement(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{relationship(edgyProps()), relationship(edgyProps())},
	}).VarLengthEdgeColumn(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeColumn = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 || len(got[0]) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeColumn = %#v, want one row of two edges", got)
	}
	for i, edgy := range got[0] {
		if edgy.Rank != int32(-3) {
			t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeColumn()[0][%d].Rank = %#v, want -3", i, edgy.Rank)
		}
	}

	// An element that is not a relationship is refused by the loop's own
	// assertion, and the refusal names the element's position — which is
	// what a caller has to tell two elements of one column apart.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{relationship(edgyProps()), node("Scalar", scalarProps())},
	}).VarLengthEdgeColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeColumn(element 1: node) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, "element 1", "expected dbtype.Relationship"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeColumn(element 1: node) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// The helper really runs per element: a relationship the entity's own
	// schema is not satisfied by fails the column, and the failure names
	// the element beside the property.
	missing := edgyProps()
	delete(missing, "rank")
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{relationship(edgyProps()), relationship(missing)},
	}).VarLengthEdgeColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeColumn(element 1: no rank) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"element 1", "decode Edgy.Rank"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeColumn(element 1: no rank) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// The same list column over a pattern admitting two edge types, which
// dispatches on the wire label per element. The column-level dispatch is
// TestEdgeUnionColumnDispatchesOnTheWireLabel's; this one is emitted by
// the element loop and is a second copy of the rule, so a label that
// picks the right helper in one says nothing about the other.
func TestVarLengthEdgeUnionColumnDispatchesPerElement(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{
			typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps()),
			typedRelationship("Edgier", map[string]any{"tag": "t"}),
		},
	}).VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 || len(got[0]) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn = %#v, want one row of two edges", got)
	}
	edgy, ok := got[0][0].(Edgy)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn()[0][0] = %T, want Edgy", got[0][0])
	}
	if edgy.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn()[0][0].(Edgy).Rank = %#v, want -3", edgy.Rank)
	}
	edgier, ok := got[0][1].(Edgier)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn()[0][1] = %T, want Edgier", got[0][1])
	}
	if edgier.Tag != "t" {
		t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn()[0][1].(Edgier).Tag = %#v, want \"t\"", edgier.Tag)
	}

	// The label picks the helper rather than the shape of what arrived:
	// Edgy's own properties under Edgier's label reach decodeEdgier,
	// which has no tag to read.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{typedRelationship("Edgier", edgyProps())},
	}).VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(Edgier: Edgy's props) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"element 0", "decode Edgier.Tag"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(Edgier: Edgy's props) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}

	// A label no candidate carries is refused by the loop's own default
	// arm, quoting both the column and the label.
	_, err = queriesOver([]string{"e"}, []any{
		[]any{typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps()), typedRelationship("Nope", edgyProps())},
	}).VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(element 1: Nope) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"e"`, "element 1", `"Nope"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("VarLengthEdgeUnionColumn(element 1: Nope) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// The nullable read of a property of no declared shape, off a
// relationship. TestAnythingSeparatesAbsentFromNull makes the same claim
// off a node, and until Edgy declared this property that was the only
// carrier the arm ever ran on — a helper shown to survive on one entity
// says nothing about another, because a helper is emitted per entity.
func TestEdgySpareSeparatesAbsentFromNullOverARelationship(t *testing.T) {
	absent, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(edgyProps()))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(no spare) = error %v", err)
	}
	if absent.Spare != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(no spare).Spare = %#v, want nil", absent.Spare)
	}

	withNull := edgyProps()
	withNull["spare"] = nil
	held, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(withNull))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(spare: null) = error %v", err)
	}
	if held.Spare == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(spare: null).Spare = nil, want a pointer to nil")
	}
	if *held.Spare != nil {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(spare: null).Spare points at %#v, want nil", *held.Spare)
	}

	withValue := edgyProps()
	withValue["spare"] = []any{int64(1), nil}
	value, err := decodeEdgy(relationship(withValue))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(spare: list) = error %v", err)
	}
	if value.Spare == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeEdgy(spare: list).Spare = nil, want a pointer")
	}
	if want := []any{int64(1), nil}; !reflect.DeepEqual(*value.Spare, want) {
		t.Errorf("decodeEdgy(spare: list).Spare points at %#v, want %#v", *value.Spare, want)
	}
}

// Two edge-union columns in one row assembly, which is the projection
// that makes the union arm's multi-column branch observable. That branch
// suffixes the arm's locals — raw, rel, ok, entity — by column position,
// and a single union column beside a column of any other kind never
// collides with anything whatever it calls them. Two of them share one
// block: unsuffixed, the second column's `raw, ok := record.Get` is a
// redeclaration of the first's and the emitted package stops compiling.
//
// So what refuses the regression here is the corpus module's own build
// rather than an assertion below, and that is the honest reading — the
// defect class is an emission that does not compile. The assertions are
// what say the two columns then decode independently, which a shared
// local would also break in the cases where it happened to typecheck.
func TestTwoEdgeUnionColumnsDoNotShareLocals(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"e", "f"}
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps()),
		typedRelationship("Edgier", map[string]any{"tag": "t"}),
	}).TwoEdgeUnionColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns = error %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	edgy, ok := got[0].E.(Edgy)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns()[0].E = %T, want Edgy", got[0].E)
	}
	if edgy.Rank != int32(-3) {
		t.Errorf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns()[0].E.(Edgy).Rank = %#v, want -3", edgy.Rank)
	}
	edgier, ok := got[0].F.(Edgier)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns()[0].F = %T, want Edgier", got[0].F)
	}
	if edgier.Tag != "t" {
		t.Errorf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns()[0].F.(Edgier).Tag = %#v, want \"t\"", edgier.Tag)
	}

	// The second column is refused on its own account, which a dispatch
	// reading the first column's binding would not do.
	_, err = queriesOver(keys, []any{
		typedRelationship("Edgy", edgyProps()), typedRelationship("Nope", edgyProps()),
	}).TwoEdgeUnionColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns(f: Nope) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{`"f"`, `"Nope"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("TwoEdgeUnionColumns(f: Nope) = %q, want it to mention %s", err, want)
		}
	}
}

// unpackableCarriers walks a bound parameter value and names every struct
// in it the Bolt packer cannot reach.
//
// The rule is packStruct's own (neo4j/internal/bolt/outgoing.go, v5.28.4
// and v6.2.0): its cases are dbtype.Point2D, dbtype.Point3D, time.Time
// and the five dbtype temporals, and its default raises
// UnsupportedTypeError. So a struct of any other named type — every gqlc
// neutral carrier among them — is a value the wire refuses.
//
// Slices and pointers are walked because packX walks them: its
// reflect.Slice arm ends in a default that packs any slice element by
// element through packV, and its reflect.Ptr arm indirects and packs what
// it finds. A carrier hidden at any depth is therefore as fatal as one at
// the top, which is why this returns every offender rather than the first.
//
// Named rather than counted, and asserted per parameter rather than over
// the whole map: a count says something was examined and an emptiness
// check over the map fires only when EVERY parameter is clean, so one
// parameter losing its widen would pass under either.
func unpackableCarriers(v any) []string {
	var found []string
	var walk func(reflect.Value)
	walk = func(rv reflect.Value) {
		if !rv.IsValid() {
			return
		}
		switch rv.Kind() {
		case reflect.Interface, reflect.Ptr:
			if !rv.IsNil() {
				walk(rv.Elem())
			}
		case reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:
			for i := 0; i < rv.Len(); i++ {
				walk(rv.Index(i))
			}
		case reflect.Struct:
			switch rv.Interface().(type) {
			case dbtype.Point2D, dbtype.Point3D, time.Time,
				dbtype.Date, dbtype.Time, dbtype.LocalTime, dbtype.LocalDateTime, dbtype.Duration:
			default:
				found = append(found, rv.Type().String())
			}
		}
	}
	walk(reflect.ValueOf(v))
	return found
}

// TestListParametersReachTheDriverPackable runs the emitted bind
// expressions and asks what the driver was actually handed.
//
// Nothing above this line reaches them. Every other query in the corpus
// is parameterless, so the whole encode direction was held by the byte
// goldens and by the compiler, and neither can see the two mistakes that
// matter: binding a temporal list bare compiles, and then the packer
// raises UnsupportedTypeError on a struct it does not know; dropping
// from<X>ListPtr's nil guard compiles, and then panics on the null the
// schema declared the parameter able to hold (bd gqlc-rw0m).
func TestListParametersReachTheDriverPackable(t *testing.T) {
	days := []Date{{Year: 2026, Month: 8, Day: 29}, {Year: 1969, Month: 12, Day: 31}}
	spans := []Duration{{Months: 1, Days: 2, Seconds: 3, Nanos: 4}}
	arg := SlotsMatchingParams{
		Tags:  []string{"a", "b"},
		Days:  days,
		Spans: &spans,
	}

	var bound map[string]any
	q := queriesRecordingParams(&bound, []string{"id"}, []any{int64(7)})
	if _, err := q.SlotsMatching(t.Context(), arg); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SlotsMatching = error %v", err)
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"tags", "days", "spans"} {
		if _, ok := bound[key]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("SlotsMatching bound %#v, which holds no %q — the rest of this test would pass vacuously", bound, key)
		}
		if offenders := unpackableCarriers(bound[key]); len(offenders) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("SlotsMatching bound %q as %#v, holding %v, which packStruct's default refuses", key, bound[key], offenders)
		}
	}

	// A list the packer walks itself is bound unconverted. This is the
	// half that is a claim about the driver rather than about gqlc: packX's
	// reflect.Slice default walks any slice through packV, and packV
	// handles every scalar kind the type map emits, so a widen here would
	// be work the wire does not ask for.
	if want := []string{"a", "b"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(bound["tags"], want) {
		t.Errorf("SlotsMatching bound tags as %#v, want %#v unconverted", bound["tags"], want)
	}

	// The temporal lists are widened per element, into the driver's own
	// array carrier. Spelled out rather than asserted shapelessly: a widen
	// that produced the right TYPES from the wrong VALUES would satisfy
	// unpackableCarriers above. Depth 1 only — ADR 0035 leaves no neo4j
	// property of a nested width for a parameter to be compared against,
	// so render_temporal.go's depth>=2 helpers have no witness here.
	wantDays := []any{
		dbtype.Date(time.Date(2026, time.August, 29, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)),
		dbtype.Date(time.Date(1969, time.December, 31, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)),
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(bound["days"], wantDays) {
		t.Errorf("SlotsMatching bound days as %#v, want %#v", bound["days"], wantDays)
	}
	wantSpans := []any{dbtype.Duration{Months: 1, Days: 2, Seconds: 3, Nanos: 4}}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(bound["spans"], wantSpans) {
		t.Errorf("SlotsMatching bound spans as %#v, want %#v", bound["spans"], wantSpans)
	}
}

// TestNullableListParameterBindsCypherNull pins the one thing the pointer
// in a nullable list parameter is for. A nil *[]Duration is the null the
// schema declared, and it has to arrive as an untyped nil — not as an
// empty list, which Cypher tells apart from null, and not by way of a
// dereference, which panics.
//
// Its own test rather than a row in the one above, because a nil here
// crashes the method: a table sharing a call would report the panic
// against whichever row ran first.
func TestNullableListParameterBindsCypherNull(t *testing.T) {
	arg := SlotsMatchingParams{
		Tags:  []string{},
		Days:  []Date{},
		Spans: nil,
	}

	var bound map[string]any
	q := queriesRecordingParams(&bound, []string{"id"}, []any{int64(7)})
	if _, err := q.SlotsMatching(t.Context(), arg); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SlotsMatching(spans: nil) = error %v", err)
	}
	value, ok := bound["spans"]
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("SlotsMatching(spans: nil) bound %#v, which holds no spans at all", bound)
	}
	if value != nil {
		t.Errorf("SlotsMatching(spans: nil) bound spans as %#v, want nil — a null the schema declared, not a list", value)
	}

	// The non-nullable lists are empty here, and empty is not null: a
	// caller who sent no elements sent a list of none. This is what stops
	// the assertion above from being satisfied by an emission that binds
	// every empty list as nil.
	for _, key := range []string{"tags", "days"} {
		if bound[key] == nil {
			t.Errorf("SlotsMatching bound %q as nil, want an empty list — the schema declares it non-nullable", key)
		}
	}
}
