// A stored value the declared width cannot hold fails the read, on all
// three paths that narrow: an entity property, a query column, and a list
// element. None of this can be established from the emission's source —
// an assertion there says a check was written, not that it fires on the
// value a graph can actually store, nor that the value it lets through
// arrives intact.
//
// The three paths are run separately because they are three emissions of
// one rule reached through different plumbing: the entity property comes
// off a Props map, the column off the driver's record, and the element out
// of a per-element loop. A check that survives one has been seen to be
// absent from another.
//
// The values here are all ones a Bolt hydrator can build. That is the
// whole premise of the defect: an INT32 property whose store holds 1<<40
// arrives as a perfectly well-typed int64, so nothing upstream of the
// conversion has anything to object to (bd gqlc-awtb).
func TestScalarRefusesAValueTheDeclaredWidthCannotHold(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		props map[string]any
		want  string
	}{
		{
			// Above int32 by a wide margin, so the round-trip clause
			// refuses it whatever the sign clause does.
			name:  "int32 above range",
			props: map[string]any{"rank": int64(1) << 40},
			want:  "decode Scalar.Rank: value 1099511627776 does not fit the declared int32 width",
		},
		{
			name:  "int32 below range",
			props: map[string]any{"rank": int64(-1) << 40},
			want:  "decode Scalar.Rank: value -1099511627776 does not fit the declared int32 width",
		},
		{
			// THE SIGN CLAUSE'S ONLY WITNESS. uint64(-1) round-trips
			// back to -1 exactly, so int64(T(v)) == v holds and the
			// round-trip clause sees nothing wrong. Only comparing the
			// signs refuses it. A mutation that deletes the sign clause
			// must kill this row and no other.
			name:  "uint64 from a negative carrier",
			props: map[string]any{"tally": int64(-1)},
			want:  "decode Scalar.Tally: value -1 does not fit the declared uint64 width",
		},
		{
			// float64's maximum overflows float32 to +Inf, and the
			// carrier held no infinity, so the conversion invented one.
			name:  "float32 overflows to an infinity",
			props: map[string]any{"weight": math.MaxFloat64},
			want:  "decode Scalar.Weight: value 1.7976931348623157e+308 does not fit the declared float32 width",
		},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			props := scalarProps()
			for k, v := range tc.props {
				props[k] = v
			}
			_, err := decodeScalar(node("Scalar", props))
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(%s) = no error, want a refusal", tc.name)
			}
			if got := err.Error(); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("decodeScalar(%s) = %q, want %q", tc.name, got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// The other side of the same check: a value the declared width DOES hold
// reaches the caller unchanged. Without these rows a decoder that refused
// every narrow value would satisfy the refusals above, and the boundary
// rows are where a check written one comparison too tight shows up.
func TestScalarAcceptsWhatTheDeclaredWidthHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		props map[string]any
		check func(*testing.T, Scalar)
	}{
		{
			name:  "int32 at its maximum",
			props: map[string]any{"rank": int64(math.MaxInt32)},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Rank != math.MaxInt32 {
					t.Errorf("Rank = %d, want %d", got.Rank, int32(math.MaxInt32))
				}
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "int32 at its minimum",
			props: map[string]any{"rank": int64(math.MinInt32)},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Rank != math.MinInt32 {
					t.Errorf("Rank = %d, want %d", got.Rank, int32(math.MinInt32))
				}
			},
		},
		{
			// MaxInt64 is the largest value a uint64 property can be
			// read back as: both agtype and Bolt integers are signed
			// 64-bit, so a larger one is unstorable rather than
			// unreadable.
			name:  "uint64 at the largest readable value",
			props: map[string]any{"tally": int64(math.MaxInt64)},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Tally != uint64(math.MaxInt64) {
					t.Errorf("Tally = %d, want %d", got.Tally, uint64(math.MaxInt64))
				}
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "float32 at its maximum",
			props: map[string]any{"weight": float64(math.MaxFloat32)},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != math.MaxFloat32 {
					t.Errorf("Weight = %#v, want MaxFloat32", got.Weight)
				}
			},
		},
		{
			// THE SPELLING PIN. This float64 is strictly greater than
			// MaxFloat32 and yet converts to exactly MaxFloat32, because
			// it lies below the rounding boundary. A check written as
			// `v > math.MaxFloat32` refuses it; the IsInf composite the
			// design prescribes lets it through. The row fails in the
			// PASS direction, which is the only direction that can
			// distinguish the two spellings.
			name:  "float32 just above its maximum, which rounds down",
			props: map[string]any{"weight": math.Nextafter(float64(math.MaxFloat32), math.Inf(1))},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != math.MaxFloat32 {
					t.Errorf("Weight = %#v, want MaxFloat32 — this value rounds down, it does not overflow", got.Weight)
				}
			},
		},
		{
			// Precision loss is not an overflow and is not refused:
			// FLOAT32 is approximate and every in-range float64 rounds.
			name:  "float32 losing precision in range",
			props: map[string]any{"weight": 0.1},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Weight == nil || *got.Weight != float32(0.1) {
					t.Errorf("Weight = %#v, want float32(0.1)", got.Weight)
				}
			},
		},
		{
			// An infinity the carrier already held is passed through
			// rather than refused: the conversion invented nothing.
			name:  "float32 from a carrier that was already infinite",
			props: map[string]any{"weight": math.Inf(1)},
			check: func(t *testing.T, got Scalar) {
				if got.Weight == nil || !math.IsInf(float64(*got.Weight), 1) {
					t.Errorf("Weight = %#v, want +Inf", got.Weight)
				}
			},
		},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			props := scalarProps()
			for k, v := range tc.props {
				props[k] = v
			}
			got, err := decodeScalar(node("Scalar", props))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("decodeScalar(%s) = error %v, want the value through", tc.name, err)
			}
			tc.check(t, got)
		})
	}
}

// The column path, which reaches the same rule through the driver's
// record rather than through a Props map. One refusal and one boundary
// pass per numeric width, because a column decode is a separate emission
// and the entity rows above carry nothing over to it.
func TestScalarColumnsRefuseAValueTheDeclaredWidthCannotHold(t *testing.T) {
	keys := []string{"id", "rank", "active", "name", "weight", "tally"}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		row  []any
		want string
	}{
		{
			name: "int32 above range",
			row:  []any{int64(7), int64(1) << 40, true, "n", 0.5, int64(1)},
			want: `ScalarColumns: decode column "rank": value 1099511627776 does not fit the declared int32 width`,
		},
		{
			// The nullable arm, which narrows inside an `if !isNil` and
			// so is a second emission of the check rather than the same
			// one. A nullable column that refuses is the shape most
			// likely to be left unchecked, since the value never leaves
			// the branch.
			name: "float32 overflows to an infinity, on the nullable arm",
			row:  []any{int64(7), int64(1), true, "n", math.MaxFloat64, int64(1)},
			want: `ScalarColumns: decode column "weight": value 1.7976931348623157e+308 does not fit the declared float32 width`,
		},
		{
			name: "uint64 from a negative carrier",
			row:  []any{int64(7), int64(1), true, "n", 0.5, int64(-1)},
			want: `ScalarColumns: decode column "tally": value -1 does not fit the declared uint64 width`,
		},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := queriesOver(keys, tc.row).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns(%s) = no error, want a refusal", tc.name)
			}
			if got := err.Error(); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(%s) = %q, want %q", tc.name, got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}

	// And the boundary values still come back through the column path,
	// so the rows above are not satisfied by a column decode that refuses
	// everything narrow.
	got, err := queriesOver(keys, []any{
		int64(7), int64(math.MaxInt32), true, "n",
		math.Nextafter(float64(math.MaxFloat32), math.Inf(1)), int64(math.MaxInt64),
	}).ScalarColumns(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns(boundaries) = error %v, want the values through", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ScalarColumns(boundaries) returned %d rows, want 1", len(got))
	}
	if got[0].Rank != math.MaxInt32 {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(boundaries)[0].Rank = %d, want %d", got[0].Rank, int32(math.MaxInt32))
	}
	if got[0].Weight == nil || *got[0].Weight != math.MaxFloat32 {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(boundaries)[0].Weight = %#v, want MaxFloat32", got[0].Weight)
	}
	if got[0].Tally != uint64(math.MaxInt64) {
		t.Errorf("ScalarColumns(boundaries)[0].Tally = %d, want %d", got[0].Tally, uint64(math.MaxInt64))
	}
}

// The list-element path, on both the entity walk and the column walk. A
// list is decoded whole, so the refusal has to name the position as the
// mis-typed-element refusal above it does — a caller told only that some
// element of a list of a thousand did not fit has been told nothing
// actionable.
func TestListyRefusesAnOutOfRangeElement(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{int64(1), int64(1) << 40},
		"blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
	}))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(ranks: [1, 1<<40]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	want := `decode Listy.Ranks: property "ranks" element 1: value 1099511627776 does not fit the declared int32 width`
	if got := err.Error(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(out-of-range element) = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}

	// The same width, one nesting of plumbing away: the nullable list
	// arm, whose elements narrow inside a different branch.
	_, err = decodeListy(node("Listy", map[string]any{
		"tags": []any{}, "ranks": []any{}, "blobs": []any{}, "stamps": []any{},
		"depths": []any{0.5, math.MaxFloat64},
	}))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("decodeListy(depths: [0.5, MaxFloat64]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	want = `decode Listy.Depths: property "depths" element 1: value 1.7976931348623157e+308 does not fit the declared float32 width`
	if got := err.Error(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("decodeListy(out-of-range depths element) = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

// The column walk's own element narrowing, which is a third emitter
// (walkListElemBody) rather than either of the two above.
//
// The width is FLOAT32 rather than the INT32 the entity rows use because
// ListyColumns projects tags, blobs and depths, and depths is the only
// narrowing element among them. One width is enough here: walkListElemBody
// narrows through a single arm whichever numeric width reaches it, so that
// arm is either checked or it is not.
func TestListyColumnsRefuseAnOutOfRangeElement(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := queriesOver([]string{"tags", "blobs", "depths"},
		[]any{[]any{}, []any{}, []any{0.5, math.MaxFloat64}},
	).ListyColumns(t.Context())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListyColumns(depths: [0.5, MaxFloat64]) = no error, want a refusal")
	}
	want := `ListyColumns: decode column "depths" element 1: value 1.7976931348623157e+308 does not fit the declared float32 width`
	if got := err.Error(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("ListyColumns(out-of-range element) = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
